note: Every word the line can say. Placeholders in {braces} are filled by reference/line-engine.js. Numbers in [brackets] are placeholders for the build to fill from data; never ship them literally. Page lines are written per role; '_' is the fallback for roles without their own line; 'untagged' is the fallback for any page that has no lines yet.

gate.lead: This page is for the team that runs the site.
gate.text: Nothing on it is hidden; it just isn't written {forAs}.

live.textOther: It's on the front page, in “Right now”.

week.textOther: This page hasn't changed for you since then.

long.lead: It's been {days} days. {countChanges} since you were here.
long.text: Rather than all of them: where it stands now, then the five that matter most {forAs}.

front.exec: No organisation has said it was broken into. Your three questions for the team are below.
front.general: Your phone and laptop are not the target: websites are.
front.security: Patch internet-facing mod_php first, then FPM. Alert on workers spawning shells.
front.journalist: 70% is a share of websites, not of the Internet. Released 21 October, not 22.
front.researcher: Two bug classes; FPM exploitation disputed; an incomplete-fix report is open.
front.everything: Every part, in the usual order. About 9 minutes.

agencies.exec: All {nAgencies} say update. {nOfflineWord}, both US, say take it offline if you can’t: decide who makes that call.
agencies.journalist: Only {nOffline} of {nAgencies} say take sites offline, both American. Don’t write “agencies say take sites offline”.
agencies.security: If you can’t patch: {nOffline} say take offline, {nIsolate} isolate, {nRestrict} restrict, {nConsider} consider, {nNone} say nothing.
agencies.general: Every government agency says the same first thing: install the fix.
agencies._: {nAgencies} agencies. All say update. They split on what to do if you can’t.

numbers.exec: Don't repeat “70% of the Internet”. The 9.2 severity holds.
numbers.journalist: 9.2 holds. 70% doesn't. “Millions” are attempts, not intrusions.
numbers._: {nFacts} facts: {nConfirmed} confirmed, {nReported} reported, {nDisputed} disputed, {nContradicted} contradicted, {nUnverified} unverified.

playbook.exec: Your team's checklist. The three questions on your front page come from it.
playbook.security: Step one: internet-facing mod_php first, then FPM, then the rest.
playbook.engineer: Targets {fixed}. An update only counts after a restart.
playbook.general: If someone hosts your site, ask them in writing whether PHP is updated and restarted.

untagged._: {pageTitle}. This page reads the same for every view; yours, {name}, is kept for the next page.
